voice.persona: Two fixed companion voices (companions.md §5): Dr. Omar, lead host — male, late 30s, friendly, confident, medium-low pitch; Noor, co-host — female, early-to-mid 30s, warm, calm, clear. Neither voice may be cloned from or resemble a real employee. Provider and voice ids pending program D10.

segments.narration: OMAR: Welcome to My Clinic. I'm Dr. Omar, a family physician at J2. Today you'll meet who we are, and the HR rules you'll actually use.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: NOOR: [[pause:0.3]] And I'm Noor, a senior nurse at J1. Nothing here is a memory test. We'll show you where to find things.
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: OMAR: [[cue:purpose]] Our purpose is simple to say and hard to do: we help people live longer, healthier, happier lives, including people who are well today. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:mission]] Our mission is to be the world's most customer-centric healthcare company. In practice, every role asks one question: did this help the patient? [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:goal]] Our goal follows from that: outstanding patient experience, alongside excellent clinical outcomes. [[pause:0.4]] Honestly, my first week here, I felt there was too much to take in. You don't need to remember everything today — just where to find it.
segments.on_screen_text: **Purpose** — helping people live longer, healthier, happier lives · **Mission** — the world's most customer-centric healthcare company · **Goal** — outstanding patient experience + excellent clinical outcomes
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: Before we start: if you had one million Saudi riyals, where would you spend it? There's no right answer. Pick whatever is closest.
segments.on_screen_text: If you had one million Saudi riyals, where would you spend it?
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: [[cue:intro]] Every clinic has values on a wall. Ours only matter if you can see them in what people do. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:collab]] Collaborative: we act together, treat everyone with respect, and stay transparent. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:resp]] Responsible: own your decisions, make things happen, and hold each other to the same standard. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:amb]] Ambitious: go above and beyond, and challenge the status quo when it stops serving patients. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:care]] Caring: act with empathy, because everyone matters. [[pause:0.4]] As you go on, think which of these you already do without being asked.
segments.on_screen_text: Values are behaviours. Open each one and look for something you already do.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: Here are six things people did this week. Match each one to the value behind it.
segments.on_screen_text: Six things people did this week. Match each one to the value behind it.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: [[cue:intro]] Strategy feels like someone else's job until you find your own work inside it. Here are the seven pillars. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:closer]] Closer: convenient access — clinics, community clinics and home health care, digital services, telemedicine. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:cure]] Cure: the best Saudi doctors, clinical outcomes, centres of excellence, prevention and wellbeing. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:cap]] Capabilities: a repeatable model for running and growing clinics, with real governance. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:culture]] Culture: our mission and values, servant leadership, a culture of excellence. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:clin]] Clinicians: a caring environment, competitive benefits, room to grow. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:care]] Care: seamless experience, empathy, loyalty built through My Care. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:cost]] Cost: competitive cost to serve. [[pause:0.4]] Whichever one you picked, that's your line in.
segments.on_screen_text: Seven pillars. Open the ones your role touches — you're not expected to memorise all seven.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: One to try. My Care follow-up calls build patient loyalty. Which pillar do they belong to?
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: [[cue:patients]] Who do we serve? First, patients and their families — sick or healthy. Many of the people who walk in today are well, and we want them to stay that way. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:community]] Second, the community around each clinic. [[pause:0.3]] [[cue:corporates]] Third, corporates and insurers. Three groups, one standard.
segments.on_screen_text: Patients & families — sick or healthy · Community · Corporates & insurers
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: We opened our first clinic in North Jeddah in 2017. [[cue:e2017]] [[pause:0.3]] In 2019 we started the employment check-up unit, [[cue:e2019]] our first corporate service. [[pause:0.3]] Then came East Jeddah, the dental centre, and Petro-Rabigh in 2023, [[cue:e2023]] our first clinic inside a corporate community. [[pause:0.3]] Riyadh followed in 2024, [[cue:e2024]] a flagship to put the brand on the map. [[pause:0.3]] The last two years added our first community clinics. [[cue:e2025]] Nine years, nine steps, one idea: bring good care closer.
segments.on_screen_text: From one clinic in Jeddah to a network across the west and Riyadh.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: You'll hear these codes every day, so it's worth knowing what they mean. Open all seven pins. J one, J two, D one, J three, J four, P-R-C and R one.
segments.on_screen_text: Seven sites. You'll hear these codes every day — open each pin.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: [[cue:ceo]] Four people lead the company. The CEO sets the direction. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:cmo]] The CMO owns clinical standards — questions about how we practise medicine land here. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:coo]] The COO runs the clinics day to day. [[pause:0.3]] [[cue:cfo]] The CFO looks after the money. You'll see their decisions in how your clinic runs.
segments.on_screen_text: Chief Executive Officer · Chief Medical Officer · Chief Operating Officer · Chief Finance Officer
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: We're proud of these, so flip them. And hold one thought alongside them. Accreditation is measured, not given. Every score here expires, and the next survey team will look at what we did this year, not at these cards.
segments.on_screen_text: Flip each card. Accreditation is measured, not given — and it has to be earned again.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: [[cue:respect]] Four values sit under everything. Respect — the rights, privacy and dignity of patients, families and colleagues. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:integrity]] Integrity — be transparent, and disclose any conflict of interest. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:accountability]] Accountability — a culture where people report safety concerns instead of staying quiet. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:innovation]] Innovation and collaboration — research and community work that improves outcomes. [[pause:0.5]] [[cue:report]] And the rule you'll use: faced with an ethical dilemma, complete an incident report within twenty-four hours and bring in the ethics team. You're never expected to work it out alone.
segments.on_screen_text: Respect · Integrity · Accountability · Innovation & collaboration · **Ethical dilemma? Incident report within 24 hours + ethics team.**
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: NOOR: Three moments now, and nobody is watching. First: you're on a panel evaluating suppliers for a clinic fit-out, and one bidder is your cousin's company. The evaluation starts in an hour. What do you do?
segments.on_screen_text: Three moments, three decisions. Nobody is watching.
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: OMAR: Nine statements from reception. Sort each: is it what the patient can expect, or what we ask of them?
segments.on_screen_text: Nine statements from the notice in reception. Sort them into the right column.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: Last one here. A patient refuses a blood test after the doctor has explained the risks. What do you do?
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: [[cue:desk]] Where help lives. First, your HR help desk — one per business unit, so you'll talk to people who know your clinic. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:oracle]] Second, Oracle. If it's a request, it goes through Oracle. That's the only way it has a record. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:pdf]] Third, the HR Quick Reference: two pages with every leave table and the pay rules. Download it now. You don't need to memorise this.
segments.on_screen_text: Your HR help desk — one per business unit · Request everything in Oracle · Full rules: **HR Quick Reference** PDF
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: [[cue:intro]] Nine types. Open the ones you need. [[pause:0.3]] [[cue:annual]] Annual: after probation, five days carried over, used by end of March. [[pause:0.3]] [[cue:sick]] Sick: valid report needed. First thirty days paid in full. [[pause:0.3]] [[cue:injury]] Work injury covers commuting, and has a same-day or next-day deadline. [[pause:0.3]] [[cue:maternity]] Maternity: twelve weeks, starting up to four weeks early. [[pause:0.3]] [[cue:exam]] Exam leave: academic exams only, documents two weeks ahead. [[pause:0.3]] [[cue:scientific]] Scientific: by profession, and can't be carried over. [[pause:0.3]] [[cue:hajj]] Hajj: two years' service and a permit. [[pause:0.3]] [[cue:compass]] Compassionate: marriage, paternity, bereavement. [[pause:0.3]] [[cue:holidays]] Then Eid, Founding Day, National Day. [[pause:0.3]] We'll practise the four people ask about most.
segments.on_screen_text: Nine types. Open the one you need — the full tables are in the Quick Reference.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: Four grades, four entitlements. Match each grade to its annual leave, in working days.
segments.on_screen_text: Four grades, four entitlements. Match each grade to its annual leave, in working days.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: One example, properly. A colleague is off sick forty days in a year, with valid reports. [[cue:s1]] First, she tells her line manager — that's first, not last. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:s2]] The first thirty days are paid in full. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:s3]] Ten days fall into the next band, and that's where pay drops. [[pause:0.4]] Note the detail people miss: it's the total in the year that sets the band, not one spell. [[pause:0.5]] [[cue:s4]] Beyond ninety days it's unpaid. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:s5]] And if the report is from outside My Clinic, the Staff Health Clinic must approve it. [[pause:0.4]] Now: what changes if her report comes from another hospital?
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: NOOR: Now you're on the other side of the desk. Four colleagues, four questions. First: Yousuf, a lab technician, wants scientific leave and already has the MD's pre-approval.
segments.on_screen_text: Four colleagues, four questions. You're the one they've asked.
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: OMAR: A short practice set now. It adapts: if you're getting these, it will finish early. If you're not, it'll keep going for a few more.
segments.on_screen_text: Answer until the practice says you're ready. It stops early if you've got it.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: [[cue:what]] GOSI is the General Organization for Social Insurance — the government body for social protection in Saudi Arabia. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:who]] It applies to Saudi employees, until retirement at sixty. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:split]] The split matters: you pay nine point seven five per cent of basic plus housing. My Clinic pays eleven point seven five. So the real contribution is twenty-one point five, and most of it isn't yours.
segments.on_screen_text: General Organization for Social Insurance · Saudi employees only · 9.75% you + 11.75% My Clinic = **21.5%** of basic + housing
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: Let's do one together. Basic four thousand eight hundred, housing one thousand two hundred. [[cue:s1]] Add them — GOSI is charged on basic plus housing, so six thousand. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:s2]] Apply your rate, nine point seven five per cent. The company's rate never touches your payslip. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:s3]] Six thousand times nought point nought nine seven five is five hundred and eighty-five riyals a month. That's the line to look for.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: Your turn. Basic six thousand, housing one thousand five hundred. What's your monthly GOSI deduction?
segments.on_screen_text: Basic 6,000 + housing 1,500. Your monthly GOSI deduction = ___ SAR
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: [[cue:elig]] One caveat before the numbers: whether you're eligible for overtime at all depends on your grade. Check that first. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:s1]] Now the arithmetic. Basic six thousand. Divide by thirty days times eight hours — two hundred and forty hours — and you get twenty-five riyals an hour. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:s2]] On a normal working day, multiply by one and a half. That's thirty-seven riyals fifty. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:s3]] On a public holiday, multiply by two. Fifty riyals an hour. [[pause:0.4]] Same hourly rate both times. Only the multiplier moves.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: One for you. Basic six thousand. You work four overtime hours on a normal working day. What's the overtime pay?
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: Six tasks, four systems. Match each one to where it actually happens. Most of them are the same system.
segments.on_screen_text: Six tasks, four systems. Match each task to where it happens.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: Let's do it once for real, on a test account. Book yourself a week of annual leave. Five steps, and I'll tell you what to look for.
segments.on_screen_text: Five steps. These screenshots come from a test account, so nothing here is real.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: One habit worth building. After you submit, open the request again. Wait until it shows as approved before you book any travel.
segments.on_screen_text: Omar's tip: Submitted isn't approved. Check the request status in Oracle before you book flights or hotels.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: True or false: if your licence expires in under thirty days without renewal, HR may suspend you from work.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: [[cue:id]] Two quick things. Your ID card: wear it where it can be seen. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:lost]] Lose it, and you email HR — there's a replacement fee. Damage it, and it's replaced free. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:wheel]] Second, what you can use from day one: health insurance, performance bonuses, development, the hybrid work policy, internal advancement and discounts. Look at the ones you'd actually use.
segments.on_screen_text: Lost card → email HR. Replacement fee ⚠ PENDING B4. Damaged card → replaced free.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: Six dress-code rules, three groups. Put each one where it applies — and pay attention to the one about casual days.
segments.on_screen_text: Six rules, three groups. Place each rule where it applies.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: [[cue:qiwa]] Two ends of one story. Starting: you accept your contract on Qiwa, the Ministry of Human Resources platform. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:oracle]] Leaving: a resignation is a request, so it goes through Oracle. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:notice]] Notice is two months, and it runs both ways. [[pause:0.4]] [[cue:eos]] End-of-service benefits and your experience certificate follow within fifteen days of your last day.
segments.on_screen_text: Accept your contract on Qiwa · Resign in Oracle · Notice: **2 months** both ways · EOS + experience certificate within 15 days
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: Last scenario. You've accepted a new job starting in three weeks. What happens with your notice?
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: Here's where you landed, objective by objective. Anything under seventy per cent has a note beside it. It's a list of where to look next, not a verdict.
segments.on_screen_text: One row per objective. Anything below 70% comes with a suggestion.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: [[cue:list]] That's the induction. You can now live the values, raise a concern the right way, answer leave and pay questions, and pick the right system. [[pause:0.3]] [[cue:pdf]] Download the HR Quick Reference. [[pause:0.3]] [[cue:survey]] And please complete the onboarding survey. Two minutes, and it shapes how we run this day.
segments.on_screen_text: You can now: live the values · raise a concern · answer leave and pay questions · use Oracle, Qiwa and Mumaris · keep your licence valid
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: NOOR: [[pause:0.3]] [[cue:next]] Next, you'll join me for clinical governance: quality, patient safety and risk. Welcome to My Clinic.
segments.speaker: noor
